message:
fix(viewer): the abandoned-list cap starts a recovery episode instead of forgetting an identity

Abandoning many AUs with no delivery in between used to grow the list without end, and every way
of bounding it that forgets a record was rejected: forgetting one means accepting it again, which
is the defect the list exists to prevent. A sequence watermark was rejected too, and rightly --
give-ups are chosen from the arrival-order head, not the lowest sequence, so a prefix rule would
block a good lower-numbered AU that simply arrived late.

The cap now starts a single recovery episode with every record kept. While it lasts no new P frame
may start an assembly (the non-key ones held at the start are dropped; they cannot come back), at
most two keyframes assemble at once, and a newer key replaces the oldest candidate while the floor
rises to it so the replaced one cannot be re-created. An assembly already in progress is answered
before the floor is consulted, so a repair is never interrupted. Before a candidate is created or
replaced the assembler asks the caller's own generation gate through an injected filter -- the
viewer passes SelectionGateState::AdmitGeneration, the Android path leaves it unset -- and a
refusal changes nothing at all: not the candidates, not the floor, not the delivery state.

The episode ends when the receiver reports that one of its delivered candidates was accepted for
decoding, right after the generation gate and the frame gate agree and before the decode itself:
the claim is acceptance, not decode success. Records that key covers are retired; if newer ones
still hold the list at the cap the episode continues. There is no timeout and no eviction.

Unit regressions cover the cap, the candidate slots and the floor, a live candidate surviving late
duplicates, release only by a delivered candidate of the right generation, the latch surviving
newer records, a refused generation moving nothing, an old sequence resetting nothing, and a
reordered lower sequence still assembling after the arrival-order head was given up. history #422.
